title: Name each WMBT with a unique step-coded URN wmbt:{wagon}:{STEP_CODE}{NNN}

facts.note: Any artifact that can contain a WMBT URN; the trigger is the URN content, not the artifact type or author.
Task text mentions creating, renaming or referencing WMBTs.
Diff-level observer needed to detect a string matching wmbt:* being created, modified or referenced in any artifact.

fires: A new WMBT is added to a wagon and given its URN
A WMBT is renamed, renumbered or moved to another wagon or step
An acceptance, doc or code file writes a reference to a WMBT by URN
Code or tooling mints a WMBT URN programmatically
doesNotFire: Edits to a WMBT's statement or acceptances that neither create, change nor reference a WMBT URN
URNs of other kinds (wagon, feature, acceptance, component) being authored

given: Any artifact (plan, wagon, acceptance, doc or code), by any author, contains a WMBT (what-must-be-true) URN.
when: A WMBT URN is created, modified or referenced.
then: The URN is a unique identifier of the form wmbt:{wagon}:{STEP_CODE}{NNN}, built via URNBuilder.wmbt(wagon_id, sequence), where wagon is the parent wagon id in kebab-case, STEP_CODE is a single step letter, and NNN is a three-digit zero-padded sequence 001-999.
prefer: Generate the URN with URNBuilder.wmbt(wagon_id, sequence) rather than hand-typing it.
Use the parent wagon's own kebab-case id as the {wagon} segment.
Pick the step letter from the step-code vocabulary (D, L, P, C, E, M, Y, R, K) and a three-digit zero-padded sequence in 001-999 that keeps the URN unique.
avoid: Reusing a URN already assigned to another WMBT (URNs must be unique).
Unpadded or out-of-range sequences (e.g. 1, 45, 000, 1000) or multi-letter / lowercase step codes.
Using a wagon segment that is not the parent wagon or is not kebab-case (uppercase, underscores, leading digit).
why: The WMBT URN is the WMBT's stable identity: it embeds the owning wagon and step code so filenames, acceptances and traceability tooling can resolve it unambiguously.
evidence: Every WMBT URN matches ^wmbt:[a-z][a-z0-9-]*:[DLPCEMYRK][0-9]{3}$ and its sequence lies in 001-999.
The {wagon} segment equals the id of the wagon that contains the WMBT.
No two WMBTs share the same URN.
verifier_detail: Term wmbt_urn = the WMBT identifier; validate with regex ^wmbt:[a-z][a-z0-9-]*:[DLPCEMYRK][0-9]{3}$.
sequence_range: 001-999 (000 is invalid even though it matches [0-9]{3}).
Valid examples from source: wmbt:resolve-dilemmas:E001, wmbt:burn-timebank:M045, wmbt:user-mgmt:C023.
